title: The Bank Robber Who Took an Uber
central_question: Dumbest Getaways 2: a bank robber who took an Uber and told it to wait, a getaway car that ran out of gas in the road, and a demand note signed with the robber's own name. Which was dumbest?
content_notes: Tone: absurd and ironic; the joke is on each scheme (a ride-share getaway, an empty tank, a signed demand note), never on a person's circumstances. Nobody is hurt in any case; no weapon and no force are shown (the Bentleyville note's claim of a weapon is not mentioned or drawn). The accused (Southfield 2022, Colma 2024, Bentleyville 2018) are never named and are drawn ONLY as dark rim-lit silhouettes tagged NOT A LIKENESS; every allegation is attributed ('police say', 'prosecutors said', ACCUSED labels, AS OF OCT 2026). The ride-share driver, the officers and the teller are generic figures; the driver is drawn only as a head shape in the car window. 'Uber' appears as plain spoken and typed text; the car is a plain unbranded sedan with no logo, livery or placard. Banks, the apartment complex, the road and the casino are generic illustrations, not the real places; no real document is imitated: the deposit slip is our own plain graphic and its demand line is a scribble because the wording was never reported. The Colma police joke is shown on a sourced label as reported, not spoken as a quote. Facts verified 2026-10-19.

lines.text: Police say he robbed a bank. By Uber.
Then told the driver to wait.
Police tracked the driver. To his home.
The getaway car ran out of gas mid-road.
The dumbest? A demand note on a deposit slip.
Then signed it. With his own name.
Arrested that evening at a casino.

claims.text: November 2022, Southfield, Michigan: police say a man took an Uber to a Huntington Bank branch on Greenfield Road and robbed it; charged with robbery; accused only, never named. Narration: 'Police say he robbed a bank. By Uber.' Headline 'GETAWAY CAR: AN UBER / TOLD TO WAIT, POLICE SAY'. The outlets differ on the date (16 vs 17 Nov) and his age (41 vs 42), so neither is stated.

Police say he asked the ride-share driver to wait outside while he robbed the bank and was driven home by the same driver, who did not know what had happened and was not involved. Narration: 'Then told the driver to wait.'

Police tracked the driver, who had dropped him at his apartment complex; he was seen walking on the property and arrested; the driver and bank employees identified him in a photo line-up. Narration: 'Police tracked the driver. To his home.'

He was arrested in the same clothes worn in the robbery, which, like the cash, were red from a dye pack a teller had put in the money; he was carrying several hundred dollars from the bank. Narration: 'Same clothes. Red dye.' Label 'A DYE PACK IN THE CASH'.

Sunday 14 April 2024, Colma, California: officers answering a reckless-driver report found a black Mercedes that had run two red lights stopped in the middle of the road near Junipero Serra Boulevard; its driver and two passengers had shoplifted from two stores on Serramonte Boulevard in Daly City (police say $1,454.33 of goods); all three booked into San Mateo County Jail; accused only, never named. Narration: 'That was not the worst.' / 'California. A shoplifting spree.'
COUNTER: 1,263 bank robberies were reported to the FBI in 2023 (of 1,362 bank crimes including 95 burglaries and 4 larcenies; the lowest total since before 1990).

The driver told officers the car was out of gas and that the two passengers were walking to get fuel; a records check showed he was a wanted fugitive from Texas. Narration: 'The getaway car ran out of gas mid-road.'

A search of the car found clothing from multiple stores with the security sensors still attached. Colma PD joked on social media that anyone planning a shoplifting spree should 'make sure your getaway car has a full tank of gas' (wording as reported in several outlets). Narration: 'Tags still on the clothes.'

Thursday 15 March 2018, about 3:40 pm, Bentleyville, Pennsylvania: police say a man handed a CFS Bank teller a demand note written on a deposit slip and left with more than $1,300; charged with robbery and related counts; ordered to stand trial in April 2018; no verdict found as of October 2026, so accused only, never named. Narration: 'The dumbest? A demand note on a deposit slip.'
FUN FACT: Friday was the busiest day for US bank crimes in 2023 with 280 of the 1,362 incidents (Monday 249, Tuesday 252, Wednesday 212, Thursday 232); 11 am to 1 pm was the busiest window (307).

Prosecutors said at the April 2018 preliminary hearing, where the note was shown, that he had signed his own name to it; police said they identified him through the signature and the surveillance video. The note's wording was not reported (the slip on screen shows a scribble, not words). Narration: 'Then signed it. With his own name.'

A friend had driven him and his girlfriend to the bank believing he was withdrawing his own money; the three went to dinner and then to the Meadows Racetrack and Casino, where police found the driver's truck and arrested him about four hours after the robbery (one outlet: 'a short time after'; the Cox report: a casino parking garage). Narration: 'Arrested that evening at a casino.'

CALLBACK: police said he used an Uber because his driver's licence was suspended and he was worried about being caught driving without one. Narration: 'Why the Uber? Licence suspended.' (the attribution is on the screen label 'POLICE SAY')
